title: Israeli strikes kill eight people in Gaza - medics say
text:
Israeli strikes kill eight people in Gaza - medics say

Ramadan Abed

Nov 1, 2026

Add AL-MONITOR on Google

Funeral of Palestinian boy Zain Owais and his father in Gaza City — DAWOUD ABU ALKAS

CAIRO, Nov 1 (Reuters) - Israeli strikes killed at least eight Palestinians, including five police officers, in the Gaza Strip in two separate attacks on Sunday, according to medics and the Hamas-run interior ministry.Medics said three people were killed in an Israeli airstrike in Gaza City. The interior ministry said the five police officers were killed in another strike in western Khan Younis, in the south of the enclave.The Israeli military said it struck several militants in Khan Younis, without giving further information. It did not immediately comment on the Gaza City strike.Israel, which says the Hamas militant group has been rearming and launching attacks in violation of a year-old ceasefire, has stepped up strikes on the group in recent weeks.Hamas has denied trying to carry out attacks or rebuild its arsenal and ​accuses Israel of undermining ​the Gaza peace ⁠deal.Last year's US-brokered ceasefire calls for eventual reconstruction of the territory. But little progress has been made as negotiators have ​failed to agree terms for Hamas to disarm or Israel ​to withdraw ⁠its troops, who control about two-thirds of the territory where they have ordered residents out.Nearly all of the more than 2 million residents live in the remaining third of the enclave among war ruins, mostly in makeshift tents and damaged buildings, still under effective control of Hamas.At least 1,500 Palestinians have been killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza since the ceasefire, according to the territory's health officials, while Israel says four ⁠soldiers have ​been killed.Palestinian authorities say more than 74,000 ​people have been killed in Israel's assault on Gaza, launched after Hamas-led fighters killed about 1,200 people ​in southern Israel on October 7, 2023. (Reporting by Nidal al-MughrabiEditing by Peter Graff)
